title: DNS & DHCP Troubleshooting
subject: DNS/DHCP Fundamentals
description: 30 enterprise tickets (15 DNS, 15 DHCP) using the 4-step triage workflow.

tickets.title: New internal host cannot be resolved by name
tickets.summary: A newly deployed internal server cannot be resolved by its hostname from client systems.

triage.q: Capture symptoms and scope. Which clients are affected and what exact lookup error occurs (NXDOMAIN, timeout, etc.)?
options: Assume it is a user mistake and close the ticket.
Confirm scope and capture exact symptoms/error text before acting.
Apply a random fix based on guesswork with no validation.
Reboot immediately without collecting any details.

diagnosis.q: State a likely root cause and the evidence you will use (zone record, conditional forwarder, cache, replication).
options: Rely only on user opinion rather than measurable evidence.
Form a likely root cause and identify specific evidence to confirm or rule it out.
Skip diagnosis and go straight to changes on production systems.
Blame the network without checking any logs or configuration.

fix.q: Document the least-risk remediation steps and how you will verify name resolution is restored.
options: Disable security controls to make the problem go away.
Declare success without testing or validation.
Apply the least-risk remediation, then verify the service is restored and document results.
Make multiple changes at once so you cannot isolate what fixed it.

workflow.changeNote: Write a change record: what changed, why, impact, and validation.

validations: nslookup resolves the hostname to the correct IP

tickets.title: Clients are not receiving IP addresses on a VLAN
tickets.summary: Clients on a specific VLAN cannot obtain an IP address and self-assign APIPA addresses.

env.Impact: No network access for the VLAN

triage.q: Confirm which VLAN is impacted and what clients report (APIPA, timeout). Capture DHCP discover/offer behavior if available.
options: Reboot immediately without collecting any details.
Apply a random fix based on guesswork with no validation.
Confirm scope and capture exact symptoms/error text before acting.
Assume it is a user mistake and close the ticket.

diagnosis.q: Identify likely cause and evidence (scope inactive, relay missing, firewall, exhaustion).
options: Form a likely root cause and identify specific evidence to confirm or rule it out.
Skip diagnosis and go straight to changes on production systems.
Blame the network without checking any logs or configuration.
Rely only on user opinion rather than measurable evidence.

fix.q: Document remediation steps and verification (renew lease, confirm correct scope options).
options: Declare success without testing or validation.
Make multiple changes at once so you cannot isolate what fixed it.
Apply the least-risk remediation, then verify the service is restored and document results.
Disable security controls to make the problem go away.

workflow.changeNote: Write a change record: what changed, why, impact, and validation.
